title: Venue
summary: Venue identifies the geographically proper court within the relevant court system. It allocates the location of litigation and is distinct from subject-matter jurisdiction and personal jurisdiction.
notes: A district need not be the single best location to be a proper venue. Conversely, a defendant’s consent to personal jurisdiction does not automatically answer every statutory venue question.

sections.Meaning: Venue identifies the geographically proper court within the relevant court system. It allocates the location of litigation and is distinct from subject-matter jurisdiction and personal jurisdiction.
sections.How to work through the question: Read the applicable venue statute, identify the defendants’ relevant residences and where substantial events or property are located, and determine whether a general or special provision governs. Bates illustrates why an event’s receipt in a district can matter.
